text:
Jamal: late-afternoon handoff — short recap of the 14:18 pager and current state

Incident Bot: [14:18] Pager: HIGH 429 rate observed on /v1/generate (service: hosted-api) — alert rule: api.429_rate.p95 > 1% for 5m

Jamal: quick timeline:
- ~14:16: small config push to autoscaler (burst window lowered from 60s -> 20s) intended to reduce cost on low-traffic shards.
- 14:18: 429 spike starts, peaking ~14:22.
- 14:23: detected KV cache evictions rising, eviction_rate x8.
- 14:25: rolled back autoscaler change and increased target replica count on affected pool.
- 14:28: applied temporary prefix-KV TTL extension to reduce cache churn.
- 14:34: routed small percentage (~10%) of traffic to fallback model-variant (quantized-v1) to reduce per-token compute.
- 14:42: 429s returned to baseline (~0.1%) and p95 latency back within SLO.

Wei: what I pulled from logs: large number of cold KV misses followed by synchronous fills that queued up. The worker batcher hit soft memory pressure and started rejecting requests (429 path). Eviction log snippet: 

```
kv-cache evict: key=prefix:abc123 size=12MB reason=memory_pressure
kv-cache miss: prefix=prompt/hash id=7f9c
batcher: queue_time=213ms mem_usage=78% rejections=12
```

Wei: repro hypothesis: the autoscaler change reduced short-term burst headroom. With a natural burst of shorter prompts, the cache churn caused multiple workers to compete to fill the same prefixes, amplifying load.

Maria: Customer impact: small number of downstream tenants saw transient 429s and ~2-3x slower tail latency for a few minutes. We saw ~1200 requests retried by our SDKs; a handful (3) of customers opened support tickets — all degraded but no data loss. Notified CS and support with the standard status blurb.

Alex: mitigation actions I executed during the window:
- reverted autoscaler config (rolled back commit f2c4a6)
- increased pool desired replica from 40 -> 60 for 10m then autoscaled down.
- bumped KV prefix TTL from 2m -> 10m to reduce fill frequency.
- temporarily allowed fallback routing (quantized-v1) for non-latency-sensitive routes.

Command snippets I ran for the rollout: 
```
# rollback autoscaler
gh pr merge --revert 1223 --admin
# scale pool
kubectl -n inference patch deployment hosted-pool -p '{"spec":{"replicas":60}}'
# extend prefix TTL via admin API
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/cache/ttl" -d '{"prefix":"/v1/", "ttl_secs":600}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
```

Jamal: current status: all metrics look normal for 30+ minutes. Secondary checks: KV eviction rate back to baseline, p95 latency under 250ms for the affected shard. No active pages.

Open items / follow-ups:
- Run focused replay of the traffic spike against a staging pool with the lowered burst window to validate the repro (owner: Wei) — ticket: INF-4821.
- Add a canary guard in the autoscaler PRs so changes to burst window require a config flag and an engineer ack (owner: Jamal) — INF-4822.
- Evaluate whether prefix-KV adaptive TTL would prevent similar churn (owner: Maria) — INF-4823.
- Customer outreach: Support will send contextual notes to the 3 customers who opened tickets (owner: Alex).

Wei: quick checklist for next oncall: watch for eviction_rate > 3x baseline, batcher.queue_time > 200ms, and 429_rate p95 > 0.5% — runbook referenced below.

Jamal: primary/secondary for the next handoff window (16:00->00:00 UTC):
- Primary: Alex (will be oncall for the next 8h)
- Secondary: Wei
- Handoff buddy: Jamal (this thread owner)

Alex: acknowledged. I'll be primary and will keep the fallback routing flag off unless more than one shard shows sustained >1% 429.

Runbook pointers / quick links: 
- KV eviction playbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction (read section "prefix-thundering")
- Autoscaler config safety: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-safety
- Incident postmortem template: https://wiki.redwood.internal/ops/postmortem-template

Maria: anything else for the handoff? I added the key graphs to the incident board and flagged the related PR for a config guard.

Jamal: nothing else. Action owners, please update the two tickets above with progress before EOD. I ran a quick `promql` query you can reuse: 
```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status="429"}[5m])) by (shard)
/ sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (shard)
```

Incident Bot: incident resolved after mitigation steps. Severity: P2.

oncall-rotation: thanks team, handing to Alex & Wei. :white_check_mark:

Alex: thanks — I'll update this thread at 18:00 UTC with a short check-in or earlier if anything pops.

Jamal: passing off. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
